- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion bias.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward to account for potential rebound or policy-driven support.
- Model frequently overreacts to recent spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3-5 days), leading to overshoot; apply dampening factor (e.g., 0.85 multiplier) to subsequent forecasts.
- In 30-day horizon, model shows persistent lag in capturing true trend — especially after sentiment shifts — so add 1-2 days of “sentiment-driven momentum” to forecast adjustment.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles (e.g., 0.67 → 0.00 → 0.67), model tends to misalign with cycle phase; adjust forecast to match sentiment phase midpoint.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome shows >10% deviation from 14-day moving average, model is likely misaligned — apply correction based on sentiment direction: bullish sentiment → +5% buffer, bearish → -5% buffer.
